description:
You are a dam safety engineer at the Indiana Dam Safety Program responding to an emergency scenario: a hypothetical dam upstream of Muncie is assessed to be at risk of failure. You must use HEC-RAS to simulate the resulting dam-break flood wave and produce an inundation severity report for emergency planners. A terminal is open in the Muncie HEC-RAS project directory.

Dam breach parameters have been placed at ~/Documents/dam_breach_parameters.txt. This document specifies the physical characteristics of the hypothetical upstream dam and the breach outflow hydrograph parameters computed using the Froehlich (1995) peak outflow equation.

Your tasks:
1. Read the dam breach parameters from ~/Documents/dam_breach_parameters.txt. The file specifies: peak breach outflow (cfs), time to peak (hours), and base duration (hours) of the triangular breach hydrograph.
2. Construct a dam-break inflow hydrograph for the Muncie boundary condition file (Muncie.b04). The hydrograph should follow a triangular shape: flow rises linearly from 0 to peak over the time-to-peak period, then recedes linearly back to 0 over the remaining base duration. Use 1-hour time intervals. Replace the existing upstream flow hydrograph with this new dam-break hydrograph. The b04 file format uses the same structure as the existing hydrograph: a header line 'Flow Hydrograph= <N>' followed by space-separated time-flow pairs, one pair per line, where time is in minutes and flow is in cfs.
3. Run the unsteady flow simulation: RasUnsteady Muncie.p04.tmp.hdf x04
4. Extract results from Muncie.p04.hdf using Python: overall peak WSE, mean peak WSE across all cells, and the timestep (in minutes from simulation start) at which peak WSE occurs.
5. Write a dam breach inundation report to ~/Documents/hec_ras_results/dam_breach_report.txt. The report must contain clearly labeled lines for: PEAK_BREACH_FLOW_CFS=<value>, PEAK_WSE_FT=<value>, MEAN_PEAK_WSE_FT=<value>, PEAK_WSE_TIMESTEP_MIN=<value>. Also include a plain-text summary paragraph (3+ sentences) describing the severity of the inundation and its implications for downstream communities.
